problem: VLM-based zero-shot ObjectNav agents reason from single frames and lack cross-step behavioral awareness, causing dead-end stalls, in-room loops and circuitous approaches to detected targets. Prompt-based history inflates token cost and cannot encode spatial signals such as angles or map cells well.
motivation: Behavioral memory is cumulative and inherently spatial, so serializing it into text grows the prompt and is lossy. Modern VLM navigators already keep a curiosity value map, which can serve as a writable medium that biases the next action immediately, persists across steps and costs no tokens.
key_idea: Insert a training-free Refinement Layer between VLM score evaluation and action execution that writes cross-step behavioral memory onto the curiosity value map through three composable skill tiers (soft scaling, lower-bound boost, hard override) in a fixed order, plus a small category-level experience prompt.
insight: Spatial behavioral memory belongs on the value map and semantic memory in short prompts. The ablation on HM3D v0.2 (Qwen2.5-VL-7B) shows the prompt channel reduces false positives (FP 10.1 to 8.9), while the Skill layer reduces max-step timeouts (MS 20.4 to 18.7) and raises SPL from 28.1 to 31.9. A fixed tier order (override > boost > scaling) gives predictable conflict resolution, so new skills can be added without retraining.
method: Panoramic pipeline: K=6 heading views are scored by a Predict VLM, ray-cast into a curiosity value map, then Plan, Goal and Action VLMs run on the chosen heading (40-step budget, WMNav-style setup).

Soft scaling: multiplies per-direction scores by gamma_k and clamps at alpha_soft=7.0. The instantiated skill is room exhaustion: when mean curiosity is below tau_exh and coverage exceeds tau_cov, explored directions are down-weighted and directions toward frontiers or exits are up-weighted.

Lower-bound boost: when the Goal VLM confirms the target at nearby pixels on two consecutive steps, the mean pixel is back-projected to a 3D anchor, and cells within radius r of it are set to alpha_max on the map, so the target is not lost.

Hard override: anti-stuck recovery monitors L2 displacement over a 2-step window and, below tau_move, forces the most open direction (score c_esc) while zeroing previously failed directions; an ABAB oscillation detector zeros directions toward the repeated waypoint.
Fixed composition: HardOverride ∘ Boost ∘ SoftScaling, with properties P1 (floor preservation), P2 (override dominance) and P3 (scaling neutrality), so new skills register by declaring their tier.

Experience prompt injection: at most L_max category-specific hints (e.g. a chair has a backrest, mirror reflections are invalid) are loaded from an offline library into the Predict and Plan VLM system prompts at O(1) token cost.

setting.action_space: discrete local motion primitives chosen by an Action VLM, with headings chosen from 6 discrete directions
setting.privileged: none (offline category hint library is used)

results: SkillNav sets new SPL state of the art on MP3D (25.5), HM3D v0.1 (39.3) and HM3D v0.2 (43.2), beating the strongest prior method MerNav (19.5, 36.9, 37.6) by up to +6.0 SPL. It also has the highest SR on HM3D v0.1 (69.7) and v0.2 (75.9), but lower SR on MP3D (48.3 vs MerNav 50.8).
limitations: Remaining errors are dominated by visual grounding on ambiguous categories (TV screen, plant, bed), which depend on the underlying VLM.
HM3D v0.1 results are computed after filtering problematic episodes, which makes comparison less clean; MP3D SR is below MerNav.
Skills are hand-designed heuristics with thresholds and a per-category hint library; evaluation is simulator-only, and the ablation covers only HM3D v0.2.
